headline: It's a trap
note: Unexpected money in your account? Never enter your UPI PIN to receive.
captionHeadline: Random money just landed in your account? Don't send it back. It's a scam.
summary: SBI is warning about the 'jumped deposit' scam. Fraudsters send you a small amount, call saying it was a mistake, then push a UPI request for a much bigger amount. Enter your PIN without checking, and the money is gone. You never need your UPI PIN to receive money.
forYou: Got a surprise credit and a panicky call? Hang up, block the number, tell your bank. Report fraud at 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
cta: Send this to your family WhatsApp group. It takes 2 seconds and could save someone's savings.

slides.label: HOW THE SCAM WORKS
slides.title: It starts with a 'gift'
points: A stranger sends a small amount to your account
They call: 'Sent by mistake, please return it fast'
Then a UPI request arrives for a much bigger amount
You enter your PIN without checking. The money is gone.

slides.label: WHAT TO DO
slides.title: Stop. Check. Block.
points: Never enter your UPI PIN to receive money
Check the amount on every request before you approve
Block the number and tell your bank right away
Report fraud: call 1930 or visit cybercrime.gov.in

slides.label: SHARE THIS
slides.title: Send this to your family WhatsApp group
slides.body: Scammers count on people trusting a phone call. Two seconds of forwarding can save someone's savings.

headline: UPI fee tomorrow
note: You don't pay it. Shops pay 0.4% on payments above ₹2,000.
captionHeadline: UPI is getting a fee from 15 October. Here's who actually pays (it's not you).
summary: From 15 October, a 0.4% merchant fee (MDR) applies to specified UPI payments to shops above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300. Fuel, railways, telecom and insurance pay a flat ₹5. Person-to-person transfers stay free, and so do shop payments up to ₹2,000.
forYou: NPCI says consumers can keep using UPI free. If a shop tries to add the fee to your bill, ask why.
cta: Send this to the friend who'll panic when they hear 'UPI fee'.

slides.label: WHO PAYS WHAT
slides.title: The shop pays, above ₹2,000
points: Most shop payments above ₹2,000: 0.4% fee
Fuel, railways, telecom, insurance: ₹5 flat
Maximum fee: ₹300 per payment (from ₹75,000 up)
Paid by the merchant, not by you

slides.label: STILL FREE
slides.title: What doesn't change
points: Sending money to a person: free, any amount
Paying a shop ₹2,000 or less: no fee
Small shops getting up to ₹1 lakh a month on QR: no fee
You, the customer: NPCI says UPI stays free

slides.label: IF A SHOP CHARGES YOU
slides.title: Ask before you pay extra
slides.body: The fee is the merchant's cost, like a card fee. NPCI's FAQ says consumers can continue using UPI free of cost. If a shop adds it to your bill, ask them to show why.

slides.label: SHARE THIS

headline: UPI fee delayed
note: NPCI says it will start immediately post Diwali. Date to be notified.
source: NPCI statement, 13 Oct 2026, via The Tribune
captionHeadline: UPDATE: The UPI fee is NOT starting tomorrow. NPCI has pushed it to after Diwali.
summary: In a statement on 13 October, NPCI deferred the 0.4% merchant fee on select UPI shop payments above ₹2,000, which was due on 15 October. It says the fee will be implemented immediately after Diwali, on a date to be notified separately. The fee has been delayed, not scrapped. Correction: our 7 am post said the fee starts on 15 October; that is no longer true.
forYou: Nothing changes tomorrow. Paying shops and sending money to people work exactly as before. Watch for the new date after Diwali.
cta: Saw a "UPI fee from tomorrow" forward? Reply with this.
correctionNote: our earlier post said the fee starts 15 Oct; NPCI has deferred it.

slides.title: NPCI hit pause two days before launch

Delayed, not cancelled

slides.label: WHY
slides.title: The festive-season push
points: Merchant groups and fintech firms asked for more time

captionHeadline: By 2050, one in five Indians could be over 60. Who will care for them?
summary: India's population aged 60 and above is projected to rise from 149 million in 2022 to 347 million by 2050. NITI Aayog estimates about 146 million people already provide untrained, unpaid care. Women spend 299 minutes a day on unpaid domestic and care work, against 97 minutes for men.
forYou: Planning for your parents' care, and your own old age, starts now.
cta: Send this to your siblings. It is a conversation worth having.

captionHeadline: SBI salary account? Your free ATM visits just got cut in half.
summary: From 1 October, SBI Salary Package account holders get 5 free transactions a month at other banks' ATMs, down from 10. Balance checks count too. After the limit, each cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST, and each non-cash transaction ₹11 plus GST. SBI's own ATMs are unchanged.
forYou: Use SBI ATMs where you can, and stop checking your balance at other banks' ATMs. Use the app instead.
cta: Tag a colleague who gets their salary in SBI.
